clauses.reason: Section 1 of Executive Order 11812 (signed October 7, 1974; 39 FR 36307) adjusts upward the rates of monthly basic pay for members of the uniformed services in the printed tables, under section 1009 of title 37 and the Federal Pay Comparability Act of 1970 named in the enacting words. The order took effect October 1, 1974 (Section 6; paraphrased because the held OCR of that sentence is garbled). The rates ran until Executive Order 11883 of October 6, 1975 (40 FR 47091, Federal Register of October 8, 1975) superseded the order. EO 11883 Sec. 5 provides that Executive Order No. 11811 and "Executive Order No. 11812 of October 7, 1974, are hereby" superseded, and EO 11883 Sec. 4, Effective Date, provides that the adjustments in monthly basic pay and basic allowances for uniformed-services members "shall be effective on October 1, 1975." Section 5 gives no separate effective date for the supersession, so it is read with Section 4: the replacement uniformed-service rates apply from 1975-10-01 and the superseded rates are replaced from that date, which is recorded as the first end. The alternative reading, that the supersession operated on the signing date 1975-10-06, is stated for the reviewer; the rates paid for 1975-10-01 to 1975-10-05 are in either case those of EO 11883. No earlier instrument ends or replaces these rates: no other held order names EO 11812 and the packet's later-event chain lists only EO 11883.

Section 2 adjusts upward the rates of basic allowance for subsistence for officers and enlisted members, with the same October 1, 1974 effective date as the whole order. EO 11883 Sec. 2 adjusts the uniformed-service basic allowances for subsistence again at its Schedule 4. EO 11883 Sec. 5 provides that Executive Order No. 11811 and "Executive Order No. 11812 of October 7, 1974, are hereby" superseded, and EO 11883 Sec. 4, Effective Date, provides that the adjustments in monthly basic pay and basic allowances for uniformed-services members "shall be effective on October 1, 1975." Section 5 gives no separate effective date for the supersession, so it is read with Section 4: the replacement uniformed-service rates apply from 1975-10-01 and the superseded rates are replaced from that date, which is recorded as the first end. The alternative reading, that the supersession operated on the signing date 1975-10-06, is stated for the reviewer; the rates paid for 1975-10-01 to 1975-10-05 are in either case those of EO 11883. First end 1975-10-01 by express supersession.

Section 3 adjusts upward the monthly rates of basic allowance for quarters by pay grade, with and without dependents, with the same October 1, 1974 effective date as the whole order. EO 11883 Sec. 2 adjusts the uniformed-service basic allowances for quarters again at its Schedule 4. EO 11883 Sec. 5 provides that Executive Order No. 11811 and "Executive Order No. 11812 of October 7, 1974, are hereby" superseded, and EO 11883 Sec. 4, Effective Date, provides that the adjustments in monthly basic pay and basic allowances for uniformed-services members "shall be effective on October 1, 1975." Section 5 gives no separate effective date for the supersession, so it is read with Section 4: the replacement uniformed-service rates apply from 1975-10-01 and the superseded rates are replaced from that date, which is recorded as the first end. The alternative reading, that the supersession operated on the signing date 1975-10-06, is stated for the reviewer; the rates paid for 1975-10-01 to 1975-10-05 are in either case those of EO 11883. First end 1975-10-01 by express supersession.

Section 4 provides that, notwithstanding the Section 1 rates, no rate of basic pay may be paid under section 5308 of title 5 in excess of the rate for level V of the Executive Schedule. It restates the limit that 5 U.S.C. 5308 itself imposes, which the footnotes of the Section 1 tables also repeat; the statutory limit continues by statute, but the order's own command is part of the superseded order and ended with it. No held source shows the limit was lifted or changed earlier. EO 11883 Sec. 5 provides that Executive Order No. 11811 and "Executive Order No. 11812 of October 7, 1974, are hereby" superseded, and EO 11883 Sec. 4, Effective Date, provides that the adjustments in monthly basic pay and basic allowances for uniformed-services members "shall be effective on October 1, 1975." Section 5 gives no separate effective date for the supersession, so it is read with Section 4: the replacement uniformed-service rates apply from 1975-10-01 and the superseded rates are replaced from that date, which is recorded as the first end. The alternative reading, that the supersession operated on the signing date 1975-10-06, is stated for the reviewer; the rates paid for 1975-10-01 to 1975-10-05 are in either case those of EO 11883. First end 1975-10-01 by express supersession.

Section 5 lists seven earlier Executive Orders on uniformed-service pay (Nos. 11414, 11475, 11525, 11577, 11638, 11692 as amended, and 11740) and provides that they are hereby superseded. The act is performed in the present tense by the order itself and the order is dated October 7, 1974, so the clause was executed and exhausted when the order was signed on 1974-10-07; Section 6 makes the order effective retroactively from October 1, 1974, and the alternative reading, 1974-10-01, is stated for the reviewer (the signing date is used because a first end cannot precede the order's own date). The later supersession of EO 11812 by EO 11883 on 1975-10-01 is not the first end of this clause, because a later supersession does not prove first cessation of a command already performed. EO 11883 does not name or revive any of the seven orders; their supersession is an accrued effect described in the savings statement.

Section 6 provides that the order takes effect on October 1, 1974 (paraphrased; the held OCR of the sentence is garbled and prints the year as '3-974'; the year is fixed by the order's own date of October 7, 1974 and the Federal Register issue of October 8, 1974). A provision that fixes an effective date operates once, when the order takes effect, so the clause was exhausted when the order was signed on 1974-10-07; the retroactive effective date 1974-10-01 is the alternative reading. The later supersession of the order by EO 11883 on 1975-10-01 is not the first end of this clause.

conflict_resolutions.QUARANTINED_RELATIONSHIP_CONFLICT: The one quarantined relationship (research/stage15/AUDIT/RELATIONSHIP_CHRONOLOGY_VIOLATIONS.csv, edge 6595) is an OFR note on EO 11778 (April 12, 1974) reading, in paraphrase, that it amends EO 11692 of December 15, 1972, which was revoked by EO 11812 of October 7, 1974. The parenthetical names this order as the later superseder of EO 11692, which agrees with EO 11812 Sec. 5 listing EO 11692; it is not an event on EO 11812 and its predecessor date is later than its actor date, so the Stage 15 audit suppressed it. It does not end or amend EO 11812.

research_rationale:
EO 11812 (signed 1974-10-07; 39 FR 36307, Federal Register of October 8, 1974, PDF pages 199-204) was read in full from the held official Federal Register text (registered as ORIGINAL:EO:11812; OCR of the 1974 scan, with garbled digits in places). Identity: the heading names Executive Order 11812, Adjusting the Rates of Basic Pay, Basic Allowance for Subsistence and Basic Allowance for Quarters for Members of the Uniformed Services, dated October 7, 1974. The dossier inventory is corrected: its Section 2 clause ran Sections 2, 3 and 4 together, and the OCR's two adjacent headings 'S E C . 5 .' and 'S E C . 6 .' had made the supersession list a mislabelled Section 6 with items (1)-(7). The corrected inventory has six clauses: Sec. 1 (basic pay tables), Sec. 2 (subsistence allowance), Sec. 3 (quarters allowance), Sec. 4 (level V limit), Sec. 5 (supersession of seven earlier orders), Sec. 6 (effective date October 1, 1974). First and whole-order end: express supersession by EO 11883 of October 6, 1975 (40 FR 47091), Sec. 5, whose Sec. 4 makes the replacement uniformed-service rates effective October 1, 1975; the Sec. 1-4 clauses end 1975-10-01 (alternative reading 1975-10-06, stated in each reason), and the Sec. 5 and Sec. 6 clauses were exhausted when the order was signed on 1974-10-07 (alternative reading: its retroactive effective date 1974-10-01), so the whole-order end is 1975-10-01, the latest first end. Authority: the order rests on 37 U.S.C. 1009 as added by Public Law 93-419 of September 19, 1974 (88 Stat. 1152, held at jobs/selden-statutes/output/texts/STATUTE-88-Pg1152.txt), under which each adjustment has the force of law and carries the effective date of the General Schedule adjustment; that statute is the authority, not an ending instrument (the dossier note that its acting text did not match by number reflects that the statute does not mention this order). The tracker's QUARANTINED_RELATIONSHIP_CONFLICT for this order is a Stage 19 count outside this claim; the held-text search of the order number finds only EO 11883 (Sec. 5) and its printed FR text, and the packet's machine searches (current-law:usc one lead, current-law:ecfr none, later-events:ofr_catalog two leads) were read with their coverage notes and name no earlier or other instrument. The original is the official FR text, so no transcription is relied on for it.

savings.reason: EO 11883 Sec. 2 adjusts again, under section 1009 of title 37, the same uniformed-service rates of monthly basic pay, basic allowance for subsistence and basic allowance for quarters from October 1, 1975, so the adjustment function continues under the successor order; pay and allowances that accrued at EO 11812's rates for periods before October 1, 1975 stay due as accrued entitlements, and the held text of EO 11883 contains no provision cancelling them. The supersession of the seven earlier orders listed in EO 11812 Sec. 5 is an accrued effect: EO 11883 does not name, revive or amend any of them. Section 5 of EO 11883 supersedes only Executive Order No. 11811 and Executive Order No. 11812, and the held text of EO 11883 has no exception or pending-matter clause for either.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1975-10-01 is the effective date of the replacement rates stated in EO 11883 Sec. 4; the supersession in Sec. 5 states no separate date and could alternatively be read from the signing date 1975-10-06.
source_notes.reason: EO 11883 Sec. 4 fixes October 1, 1975 as the effective date of the replacement uniformed-service pay and allowance rates; Sec. 5 supersedes EO 11812 without its own effective date, so the supersession is read with this date.
